jewelry.name: brosch, brooch
jewelry.title: brosch, brooch
jewelry.reason: The image shows a silver openwork brooch in a cross/heart motif, a well-documented type of Iroquois (Haudenosaunee) silver jewelry; the record explicitly ties it to a Seneca/Oneida woman, supporting the Seneca attribution.

jewelry.name: Brooch
jewelry.title: Brooch
jewelry.reason: A simple silver brooch (sewn/ring type) collected directly from Sarah Taylor, a Seneca woman at Cattaraugus, New York — a well-documented Iroquois silver jewelry form with clear provenance to the named individual.

masks-ritual.name: mask, ga gó said
masks-ritual.title: mask, ga gó said
masks-ritual.reason: This is a classic Iroquois (Seneca) False Face Society mask — carved wood with metal eye plates, horsehair, and a twisted-mouth face — used by medicine practitioners in healing ceremonies, matching the claimed ethnicity precisely.

masks-ritual.name: mask, ga go sa
masks-ritual.title: mask, ga go sa
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden "false face" style mask with eye/mouth holes and cloth strips for tying, described as used by a Seneca mask society (Cattaraugus) — this is a classic Haudenosaunee/Seneca False Face Society ritual mask.

photo.name: photographic print; carte-de-visite
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); carte-de-visite
photo.reason: A studio carte-de-visite portrait of Lewis "Deerfoot" Bennett, a Seneca man, in fringed frock coat, leggings, moccasins, and ear ornaments beside an animal skin—a documentary photo of Seneca dress.

instruments.name: skallra, turtle shell rattle, Kanyáhte’ ká’nowa’
instruments.title: skallra, turtle shell rattle, Kanyáhte’ ká’nowa’
instruments.reason: A turtle-shell rattle with a wooden handle, documented as collected from Lyman Smith, a Seneca individual from Cattaraugus, and used by the False Face mask society and Feather Dance — a well-documented Seneca/Haudenosaunee instrument type.

instruments.name: Skög, turtle shell rattle, Kanyáhte “ká” nowa’, o ná gaa gus ta wen sä
instruments.title: Skög, turtle shell rattle, Kanyáhte “ká” nowa’, o ná gaa gus ta wen sä
instruments.reason: A turtle shell rattle with wooden handle, used in Iroquois/Seneca ceremonial societies (e.g., False Face Society, Great Feather Dance), matches known Seneca ritual instrument traditions.

garment.name: Moccasins
garment.title: Pair of Moccasins
garment.reason: A pair of native-tanned hide moccasins with quillwork and beaded cuffs, consistent with Haudenosaunee/Seneca footwear and craft traditions; clearly a garment worn by the people.

garment.name: headgear, cap, heater, bonnet
garment.title: headgear, cap, heater, bonnet
garment.reason: A beaded feather headgear/cap collected directly from Levi Cook, a named Seneca individual at Cattaraugus, with beadwork typical of Haudenosaunee-style caps — strong direct provenance to the claimed people.

garment.name: Moccasins
garment.title: Pair of Moccasins
garment.reason: A pair of soft-soled hide moccasins with quillwork beaded cuffs in floral/geometric motifs, consistent with Iroquoian (Seneca) footwear traditions and directly matching the claimed garment type.

arms.name: club
arms.title: club
arms.reason: The image shows classic gunstock-style war clubs with curved wooden bodies, ball/knob heads, and iron blades or spikes set into the stock — a well-documented Iroquoian (including Seneca) weapon form, consistent with the museum's attribution.

sculpture.name: Doll
sculpture.title: Mother-and-Child Doll
sculpture.reason: This is a classic corn-husk-faced doll with a wooden/husk head, cloth garments, beadwork trim, and a cradleboard-carried baby, consistent with Seneca/Haudenosaunee doll-making traditions using beaded cloth clothing and corn-husk construction.

household.name: Träskål, kärl, skål, vessel
household.title: Träskål, kärl, skål, vessel
household.reason: A wooden burl-style bowl with two small lug handles, a form consistent with Iroquois (Seneca) wood carving traditions; the museum record labels it Seneca/Iroquois League material. Though claimed as "ceramic," the object is clearly carved wood.
